beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps a dense carrier while a compact DQ-CTM process updates it through shared recurrent ticks.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: The method is organized around a dense carrier rather than a single compact state. The encoder turns the low-resolution image into features. Windowing breaks that field into local token groups. DQ-CTM reads and updates the carrier through repeated shared ticks. The decoder maps the updated dense field back to a super-resolved image.

params.headline: ThinkSR runs a dense carrier through shared thought ticks
params.note: The recurrence stays inside the thought stage.

beats.intent: The carrier starts as encoder features, and window partitioning preserves the dense token field for thought updates.
beats.narration: The equation defines the dense carrier before the recurrent thought process touches it. The feature field is what persists spatial detail. The encoder builds it directly from the low-resolution input. The token set is the windowed form consumed next. The window operator partitions the field without dropping tokens.

params.headline: The encoder builds the field that windowing preserves

window partition of the dense field

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest lightweight model in the comparison; its parameter count is second largest among the five methods.
beats.claim: ×4 lightweight super-resolution, average over five benchmarks.
beats.narration: The parameter comparison is about model size, not score. CATANet is the smallest at zero point five three five million parameters. RFDN and IMDN remain below one million parameters. DQ-CTM-SR uses one point one two nine million parameters, making it the second largest of the five. CARN is larger still at one point five nine two million parameters.
